questions.prompt: Input width 64, kernel 5, stride 2, padding 2 on each side, dilation 1. What is the output width? (integer)
A 3x3 convolution maps 32 channels to 64 channels, with bias. How many parameters? (integer)
Stack of four layers: 3x3 s1, 3x3 s1, 3x3 s2, 3x3 s1 (no dilation). What is the receptive field of the last layer's units? (integer)
What does weight sharing in a convolutional layer mean?
options: Different layers use identical weights, which cuts the model size to a single layer's worth
Weights are shared between the training set and the test set during every forward pass
All channels share one bias term, so that there is only a single bias for the whole layer
The same kernel weights are used at every position, so parameters do not depend on image size
questions.explanation: One kernel slides over the whole input; its gradient sums contributions from all positions.

questions.prompt: An object shifts 5 pixels to the right in the input. For a convolutional layer (ignoring borders) the feature map...
options: changes in an unpredictable way, because the kernel breaks the layout
shifts correspondingly (equivariance), it does not stay the same
is mirrored left to right, because the kernel is flipped in convolution
stays exactly the same (invariance), so the output ignores the shift
questions.explanation: Convolution commutes with translation; invariance requires pooling or aggregation.
